ZeroOps · Jev in incident triage

AI agents for incident response became a real category in 2026, yet the routine judgment calls in incident management (is it real, whose is it, how bad, act or page) still sit with hand-written rules and whoever is on call, in application incidents and network monitoring alike. This demo shows what a typed decision model, TypeSafe's Jev, can do in those calls: 12 typed questions per incident in one call, answers with probabilities, and the act-or-page gate written in ordinary code, run on 56 synthetic incidents. The material ends with the value it could have and a staged way to test it on real tickets.

What the demo measured · Our measurement
  • Jev (TypeSafe API) proposed the same first action as our label on 28 of 56 synthetic incidents (50%). A looser score that also accepts alternatives we listed after the first run gives 52 of 56 (93%).
  • The gate let it act alone on 22 of 56, none of them among the 20 incidents we labelled unsafe to automate. Those 20 come from only 5 scenario types, so the 95% upper bound on the unsafe rate is still 43%.
  • Most of those calls were close: 18 of the 22 passed the "page a human?" check with a probability between 0.73 and 0.88, against a cut-off of 0.90. With the cut-off at 0.80 it would have acted alone on 12, at 0.85 on 17.

The incidents were written and labelled for the demo from 14 templates with explicit clues, and there is no held-out set, so they show the mechanism and your own tickets are the real test. The results report has every table and its definitions.

See it work

Threshold Lab

Change the gate's thresholds and see which of the 56 recorded decisions move between act, page and log. The model's answers were recorded once and stay fixed; only the code's decision changes. Shows exact and acceptable action side by side, real incidents logged as noise, and a sweep of the "page a human?" cut-off.

One incident, two kinds of output

One recorded call each to Jev (12 typed questions) and to openai/gpt-4o-mini (5 JSON fields) on INC-0001. Both gave the same category, root cause and first action. The page shows what each hands back for a gate to check: Jev attaches a probability to each answer, the chat reply carries values only. One pair of calls, so the timings are illustrative.

Rebuild these pages from the saved results, with no API calls: ./jev/bin/python scripts/run_all.py --skip-api --skip-local. Re-running the evaluation, re-recording the two-outputs page (--race-live) or remaking the videos (--videos) calls paid APIs; README.md lists which step costs what.

Data: 56 synthetic incidents (14 templates × 4 variants), corpus version 0b4839761e06, decision logs written 4 Oct 2026. Models: Jev (TypeSafe API) jev-1.13.0; Jev (via OpenRouter) typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917; Kev-4B (local GPU) kev-latest; Laya (local GPU) typed-decisions.

Every file in this folder, in reading order, with sizes and build dates: README.md. A PDF of the deck for quick viewing: 1_ZeroOps-Jev_v4.pdf; slide images, video frames and page screenshots: previews/.

This folder works on its own. To serve it, from the project root: python3 -m http.server --directory outputs --bind 127.0.0.1. The files under docs/ are copies made by scripts/build_hub.py; edit the originals in inputs/research/. Don't serve the project root, which holds .env.
